transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. I came in today because... well, I know this might sound a little hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced lately that one of my MBA classmates and a startup advisor I know are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. It's like... certain comments they make in class, or even just regular Slack messages, feel like they're actually coded signals about where my career is supposed to go.
Have you been feeling unusually energized or irritable, or perhaps significantly depressed or hopeless, during the time you've been having these thoughts?

Well, I definitely wouldn't say I've felt depressed. If anything, it's been the opposite. Most days I've felt unusually switched on and just really optimistic. It's like I'm right on the edge of something huge happening for me. But at the same time... I guess I have been a bit irritable. I've found myself snapping at my project teammates, or even my boyfriend, over really small delays that normally wouldn't bother me at all. I just feel like things need to move faster.
Have you experienced these specific thoughts about your classmates and the coded signals during times when your mood felt completely normal and you weren't feeling especially energized or irritable?

No, I haven't. Um, before this whole stretch of being so energized and driven, I never had messages feel coded like this... or heard my name being called when no one was actually there. Those specific experiences really only started once my mood, and I guess the intensity of my workload, shifted after I began my MBA prerequisites. When I felt normal before all this, none of that was happening.
About how many days in a row have you been feeling this unusually high energy and optimistic mood?

Well, it's been a lot more than just a few days. I'd say... it's been going on for about two months straight now. It basically started right around the time I began my part-time MBA prerequisite program, while I was still keeping up with my regular operations job.
